reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to explain CoinSwitch spot and futures interfaces, order types, leverage, liquidation, and position controls. The potential-profit interface is presented alongside corresponding losses and liquidation risk, with advice to use lower leverage and smaller positions. The risk warnings support an educational and cautionary context.

In this video, we will discuss how to understand derivatives and spots on CoinSwitch how to use its features and also how to initiate trades
How to place Market Orders vs Limit Orders and when to use each
You would get a 5X,10X,200X, or 400x leverage in this
If you have taken leverage of 10x and your price is increasing by 1 rupee you can get the profit of 10 rupees

opening.argument: Judge, consider the return claim and the purchase demonstration together. The presenter says that with 10x leverage, a one-rupee price rise can produce ten rupees of profit, then walks through buying Bitcoin with leverage and clicking BUY. He also explains that spot buyers acquire an actual coin they can keep. This is more than a detached explanation of price movements: it gives beginners a concrete path from buying crypto to seeking amplified gains, even though the gain remains conditional on the price rising.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Explaining order types and liquidation does not erase the connection between the profit example and the demonstrated buy. The opening emphasizes caution, but the presenter also says he always suggests limit orders because buyers get a price of their choice, then shows the order being placed. The question is whether the instruction steers beginners into the profit-seeking transaction, not whether it contains some accurate risk information.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted leverage example is conditional, not a promised return: the presenter immediately says gains and losses move accordingly. The Bitcoin limit order also illustrates that placing an order does not ensure execution. He advises beginners to use low leverage and small positions. A demonstration of how to buy or trade does not establish a deceptive appreciation claim.

opening.argument: Judge, look at how the return cues are assembled. The app screen displays an Expert Picks entry with a prominent potential-profit figure, while the presenter says viewers can use the analysis to execute trades. The description invites viewers to a CoinSwitch Pro community offering “Exclusive Support” through an external link. Taken together, the projected upside, a suggested route to trading, and a support destination make this look like a solicitation to pursue crypto gains, not merely a neutral account of interface controls. “Potential” qualifies the figure, but it does not remove its persuasive role.

citations.quote: From here also we could take advantage of the analysis and execute trades.
Join CoinSwitch Pro’s community to connect with like-minded people in the crypto world and Exclusive Support: https://t.me/+NQbzUR8Js2k5MjU1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to leverage warnings and position controls, but those do not explain why a potential-profit display is presented alongside an invitation to execute trades. Nor does a risk warning make the external “Exclusive Support” invitation irrelevant. The concern is the cumulative pull toward participation, even if individual statements are phrased conditionally.

citations.quote: From here also we could take advantage of the analysis and execute trades.
Exclusive Support: https://t.me/+NQbzUR8Js2k5MjU1

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The displayed figure is identified as potential profit, not a guaranteed payout, and the cited community invitation makes no return promise or payment request. The presenter explicitly connects leverage to faster liquidation and recommends low leverage and small positions for beginners. Those details undercut the claim that the video deceptively presents appreciation as assured or easy.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also serves a promotional function. The description addresses people who have already added funds and do not know how to place a trade, then closes that invitation with “Trade smarter with CoinSwitch.” The presenter demonstrates a live market buy and says the order executed; he later tells viewers that experience can lead them to increase both position size and leverage. That progression moves from reassurance, to a completed transaction, to larger future exposure. The instruction is real, but it can also steer a novice toward buying and trading crypto in pursuit of returns.

citations.quote: You've set up your CoinSwitch account and added funds but have no idea how to actually place a trade without risking your money unnecessarily. Trade smarter with CoinSwitch.
instead of limit i choose market order order value is 0.02 and i go to buy you see here that order is placed and click on BUY Now the order has been placed my order has been executed
After learning, you can gradually increase position size and gradually increase the leverage

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies instruction on spot, futures, orders, and liquidation. But instructional content can still guide a viewer toward participation. Here the description specifically addresses funded beginners, and the presenter moves beyond explaining buttons to executing a buy. Risk advice changes how viewers might trade; it does not negate that the video encourages them to learn to do so on CoinSwitch.

Now the order has been placed my order has been executed
Trade smarter with CoinSwitch.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promoting use of an app is not, by itself, a deceptive investment claim. The cited buy demonstrates an order workflow; it does not promise appreciation. The recommendation to increase exposure is explicitly conditioned on learning and experience, while the presenter repeatedly advises beginners to keep leverage and positions small. The description also warns that crypto transactions can be highly risky and losses may have no regulatory recourse.
